newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Miners blast Indonesian move on Busang gold find.
newsitem.headline: Miners blast Indonesian move on Busang gold find.

text.p: The Indonesian government's attempt to force a settlement over the spectacular Busang gold find was criticised by local miners on Wednesday, who said the move could hurt investment in mining.

Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd, which owns the dominant share in the Busang field, said on Tuesday that it has been advised by the Indonesian government to reach a settlement with Barrick Gold Corp, also of Canada, by December 4.
Indonesia wants Barrick to take a majority 75 percent stake in Busang in East Kalimantan with Bre-X holding 25 percent, the Calgary, Alberta-based Bre-X said on Tuesday.
Bre-X also said the Ministry of Energy and Mines "would appreciate if the parties could consider a 10 percent participation being given to the Indonesian government."

The company said if no deal was reached by December 4, the Indonesian government would take steps "to prevent a delay in the development of Busang", estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 47 million ounces of gold.
Mining industry sources said the Indonesian government's move to recommend a partner of its choosing to Bre-X was unprecedented.
"It is wrong," one industry source said. "In my 30 years in the mining sector, I have not seen anything like this."
"This will certainly dampen the investment climate in the mining sector," the source said, declining to be identified.
"Miners will become cautious when wanting to invest in the sector because an element of uncertainty could arise when they discover a large ore body," he said.
Another source said the issue had been further complicated by the involvement of President Suharto's children.
Bre-X has entered into a partnership agreement with PT Panutan Duta of the Panutan Group run by Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto.
Under this agreement, PT Panutan would receive $40 million over 40 months plus a 10 percent stake in the richest parts of Busang.

Barrick has teamed up with a construction company in the Citra Group of Suharto's eldest daughter, Siti Hardianti Rukmana, in what Barrick had said was a partnership "to prepare us for a potential mining development project".

"Small miners will be scared off by this development because some players might just jump into the picture midway," the second source said. "I foresee legal action being taken and the case dragging on for some time."
He, however, did not consider the government's request for a 10 percent stake in Busang as being unusual as miners usually allocated shares to state-owned companies.
Meanwhile, local businessman Jusuf Merukh, who claims 40 percent of Busang, said on Wednesday he had delayed a $1.9 billion lawsuit against Bre-X, to settle their ownership dispute, until December 4.
"Bre-X has asked me to extend my (lawsuit) deadline to December 4 (from November 22)," he said. "It's because they are busy...possibly because of the talks with Barrick."

Merukh said the talks between Bre-X and Barrick could be over a partnership to operate Busang as neither he nor Bre-X had the expertise, adding that this would not affect his 40-percent ownership claim.
The U.S.-educated Merukh said he expected his ownership dispute with Bre-X to be resolved before Christmas.

The director-general of mines, Kuntoro Mangkusubroto, was last month abruptly stripped of his powers to approve mining contracts of work following his decision to delay awarding Bre-X the contracts until the firm resolved its dispute with Merukh.
Mines Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana confirmed revoking Kuntoro's powers but denied it was linked to Bre-X.
